title: myCareer corpus
description: High-fidelity career record. Captured at autobiography depth, verified per fact type, rendered on demand into resumes, profiles, letters and interview answers. See docs/mycareer.md.

id.description: Stable, human-readable id. Prefix by entity type: org. role. sys. clm. fig. sto. reg. ev. att. rec. rej. oq. ses.

ym.description: Year or year-month. Day precision is almost never sourceable and invites contradiction.

fact_type.description: The kind of fact a piece of evidence can establish. Verification is per fact type, never per person.

tier.description: T0 asserted / T1 self-confirmed with a novel detail / T2 documented / T3 corroborated by a named person / T4 independent record. T1 is the floor for anything rendered.

status.description: Only 'confirmed' may be rendered. 'open' covers PARTIAL and DON'T RECALL. 'rejected' is permanent and drives DO-NOT-CLAIM.

credential_suffix.description: e.g. MBA. Rendered in letterhead; suppressible per target.

public_name.description: Use when the org may not be named directly; see disclosure_limits.

size.description: Headcount or revenue band at the time, not today.

nameable.description: False when NDA or clearance forbids naming the org in renders.

title_history.description: Prior titles in the same role, for promotion narratives.

public_title.description: Alternate title when the real one triggers a screen. Must remain truthful.

location.description: City, ST. Required by the autobiography chapter headings.

concurrent.description: Overlaps another role. Must be disclosed as such in long-form documents.

span.description: Applications, products, regions, or business units owned.

chapter.description: Autobiography-depth narrative for this role: the state it was in on arrival, what was inherited, the arc, what changed, and the capability it added. This is what the Career Autobiography renders from.

departure_framing.description: Agreed phrasing for why the role ended. Never rendered verbatim; guides tone.

role_ids.description: A system may span roles and even employers. This is why systems are first-class.

purpose.description: What it did and for whom.

reconstruction.description: Autobiography-depth technical narrative: architecture, data model, failure modes, what would break at 10x, what you would build differently.

money_movement.description: Rails, if any: ACH, card, wire, RTP.

contractual_overlays.description: Prime or sub on federal contract, BAA, DPA, customer security addenda, scheme rules.

seat.description: Where the subject sat relative to this system.

scale.description: figure ids: users, volume, data size, throughput.

text.description: Flat, neutral, no adjectives. This is the sentence sent to an attester -- never the polished bullet.

narrative_long.description: Autobiography depth: the situation, what was actually done, who else was in it, what it changed, in the subject's voice. Captured FIRST; everything shorter is derived from it.

narrative_short.description: Two or three sentences. KSA evidence paragraphs and LinkedIn render from here.

bullet.description: Resume-length compression. Derived from narrative_long, never written first.

constraint.description: The pressure that made this necessary: budget cut, headcount freeze, audit finding, regulatory gate, deadline. Achievements are framed by their constraint, not as transformation leadership.

agency.description: Did it / scoped it and handed off / enabled a team to execute. Never allowed to drift upward.

authority.description: Authority is not influence. Four different claims.

confirmed_detail.description: The particular the subject supplied that the scaffold did NOT contain: a person, a date, an artifact name, a number, a fight. Required for status=confirmed. This is what separates recognition from suggestion.

job_families.description: Families this claim legitimately supports, e.g. engineer, product_manager, delivery_program_manager, architect, engineering_leader, executive.

suppress_for.description: Targets where this claim hurts: executive scope on a hands-on IC search, P&L on an architect role. Resolves the Phase 6 / executive-letters tension as a filter instead of a rewrite.

knowledge_currency.description: Computed against dates and regime revisions. A framework claim from 2016 is not a claim about the 2024 revision.

unit.description: USD, USD_millions, people, percent, months, transactions, TB, requests_per_second.

kind.description: What the number measures: investment_secured, cost_removed, headcount, uptime, cycle_time.

baseline.description: What it was before. A number without a baseline is decoration.

instrument.description: How it was measured, and by what system.

source.description: Where it can be produced from: board deck, audit report, finance system, contract.

sourceable.description: Can the subject actually produce the source today? Unsourceable numbers are omitted, never softened.

composite_of.description: Components of a composite headline figure. Must decompose cleanly; the validator checks the arithmetic.

headline.description: One of the 4 to 6 numbers that carry the story and appear in the first 25% of a document.

before_state.description: In terms a skeptic could picture.

personal_action.description: What the subject personally did, distinct from the team, a vendor, or a predecessor.

decision.description: The call a competent peer might have made differently.

tradeoff.description: What was accepted, deferred, or risk-accepted, and by whom.

what_went_wrong.description: What failed or was left undone. Its absence is what makes an answer sound rehearsed.

contradiction_risk.description: Who could contradict this account and what they would say. Interview preparation depends on this field.

spoken_90s.description: Rendered interview answer, in the subject's voice, built only from confirmed material.

why_attached.description: The one-line reason it applied given the system described.

observable.description: The artifact, auditor, gate, clause, or recurring meeting that confirms it.

accountability.description: Four different claims. Never collapse them.

revision_known.description: Which revision of the framework the subject actually worked under.

adjacent_ids.description: Regimes sharing evidence, control work, or calendar. Populated from data/adjacency.json.

producible.description: Can the subject actually retrieve this today?

claim_ids.description: Request narrow. Broad attestation requests go unanswered and are worth less when answered.

contact_ref.description: Reference or hash, not a raw address in the corpus.

scope.description: What this person can actually speak to. Attesting outside scope is worth nothing.

strength.description: Hearsay never raises a tier. It is recorded for reference planning.

verifies.description: The fact types this record actually establishes. An IRS transcript verifies employer, dates and compensation -- never accomplishments. The validator enforces this.

document_ref.description: Pointer into a secure store. The document itself never lives in the corpus.

conflicts.description: Where this record disagrees with stated history. Produces an open question, never a silent overwrite.

by_fact_type.description: Per-fact-type tiers. The top-level tier is the MINIMUM across these, never the maximum -- a claim is only as verified as its weakest rendered component.

text.description: The candidate that was rejected, kept verbatim so it is never re-proposed.

close_action.description: The specific thing that would close it: a document to find, a person to ask, a system still accessible. Not 'think about it more'.

tagline.description: One positioning line for letterhead. Never list three titles.

carries.description: The two or three claim ids that carry the case.

suppress.description: Claims that become noise or trigger an overqualification screen.

objection.description: The obvious objection a hiring manager raises.

fit.description: Say so plainly when the fit is thin.

workaround.description: The generic phrasing that is permitted, e.g. 'a federal civilian agency' instead of the agency name.

subject.description: The system, program, role, or claim set interrogated.

next_scaffold.description: Branches not yet walked, ranked by likely payoff.
